newsitem.title: USA: Marhsall & Ilsley to buy Security Capital for $945 million.
newsitem.headline: Marhsall & Ilsley to buy Security Capital for $945 million.

text.p: Marshall & Ilsley Corp., a Wisconsin-based bank, said it plans to acquire Security Capital Corp. for $945 million, strengthening its presence in Milwaukee and other parts of the state.
The purchase price will consist of Marshall & Ilsley common stock and $376 million in cash worth a total of about $945 million, or $92 a share, the company said in a statement.

"The addition of Security will strengthen M&I's presence within our Wisconsin banking region, particularly the metropolitan Milwaukee area," Marshall & Ilsley Chairman James Wigdale said. The combined company will have total assets of $18.5 billion.
The companies plan to close, sell or merge some branches where overlap exists and cut about 450 jobs, most of those through attrition or retirement.

Milwaukee-based Marshall & Ilsley, with $14.8 billion in assets, owns 29 banks with about 225 offices in Wisconsin and a Phoenix, Ariz., bank with 12 branches. It also provides trust and investment management, mortgage banking and other financial services in 54 offices across the country.
Security Capital's Security Bank has 42 branch offices and 10 lending offices throughout Wisconsin.
The acquisition will add to earnings in 1998, Marshall & Ilsley said but did not elaborate. Officials were not available to comment further at either company.
Marshall & Ilsley said it will decide which branches to close or sell within 60 days. It did not say whether the moves would result in a charge to earnings.
Marshall & Ilsley stock closed at $37, up 31.25 cents, and Security Capital stock closed at $84.50, both on Nasdaq on Friday.
The acquisition is subject to approval by regulators and shareholders and is expected to be completed by Oct. 1, the company said.
